To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) branched DNA molecules interact with drugs differently than unbranched duplex molecules of similar sequence and that (ii) the major site of enhanced drug binding in a specific case is the branch point itself.

(i) the junction of a DNA branched structure is a site of enhanced binding by intercalating drugs, (ii) the binding is not due to a general increase in the number of intercalation sites, and (iii) the binding is localized to a region that is centered on the junction and extends about 4 bp on each side of the branch site.
a drug binding site in a DNA molecule is located precisely at the junction between the two arms of the molecule and that the binding is highly specific for the branched DNA structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to the study of DNA-drug interactions.
the use of chemical footprinting techniques to study the interactions of drugs with DNA, in particular the binding of intercalators to a junction of four DNA strands.
the use of chemical footprinting to study the interaction of DNA with intercalators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the junction site has an enhanced propensity to intercalate drugs.
the junction is a site of enhanced binding, with a pattern of cuts which is not simply the sum of the two duplex controls and which is distinct from the pattern obtained with linear duplexes.
the junction region is the site of the drug interaction, but the exact nature of the interaction is still unclear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the junction structure is not simply an extended duplex, as was previously assumed, and that its properties are not easily predicted on the basis of the properties of the duplexes of which it is made.
a drug binding site in a junction is located at or very near the branch point.
the branched junction structure has a site for drug binding that is different from any of the control duplexes, with the major site being at the junction point.
The main takeaway from our work is that
branched DNA molecules are more sensitive than linear duplexes to intercalation by a variety of intercalating drugs and that the site of interaction is located at the branch site.
branched DNA molecules are a useful tool to probe the nature of drug binding to duplex DNA.
the binding of intercalators by DNA is a complex process that depends on the structure and flexibility of the molecule.
